title: Stars trails over La Silla
caption: Star trails and the Magellanic Clouds over La Silla Observatory, Chile
celestial: Photograph taken at La Silla Observatory, Chile

recognition.text: Published in the ESO image archive. No published rating.

story: Stars wheel around a single point in the sky above a telescope dome at ESO's La Silla Observatory. On the left, a lighter, hazy patch softens the darkness. The picture was built from a long series of night exposures taken looking south.

The trails reveal the sky's apparent motion, which is really Earth turning on its axis. Every star seems to circle the celestial south pole, which appears here on the right, just above the dome in the foreground. The nearer a star lies to that point, the smaller the circle it traces.

The diffuse glow on the left comes from the Large and Small Magellanic Clouds. These are two irregular galaxies that are neighbours of the Milky Way. Each is a galaxy in its own right, lying outside the Milky Way, and from La Silla they appear as a soft, lighter area in the southern sky.

understand.summary: This is a series of night-time photographs taken in visible light with a camera at La Silla and combined into one image. The exposure settings and colour processing are not published.
understand.eye: The eye sees stars as fixed points; only a camera combining many exposures can record the sky's rotation as circular trails.

explore: Photographs pointed at the celestial pole are a favourite of night-sky photographers, because the concentric circles show at a glance how the whole sky appears to pivot around one spot as the planet spins.
alt: Circular star trails centred on a point above a telescope dome, with a lighter hazy glow on the left.
